title: I built a free-form woodworking prototype in Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol
author: biblibubli
selftext:
I’ve been working on this for about two weeks.

The goal was to make a piece of wood you can actually cut into however you want. The whole thing is built around an editable SDF, so the geometry really changes as you carve it.

I did most of the work in Codex using GPT-5.6 Sol. I have some programming and CS background, but not years of graphics-programming experience, so my role was mostly to understand the options, choose a direction, and decide whether the result actually made sense for the game.

Sol was great at going deep into the technical parts: SDF math, ray tracing, geometry, sparse GPU storage, grid density, memory tradeoffs, and all the annoying details around keeping an editable volume on the GPU without burning a stupid amount of VRAM.

It was also useful for brainstorming weird problems. For example, I wanted the wood shavings coming off the chisel to curl, so we explored representing them as SDF geometry and wrapping them along an Archimedean spiral.

The part I found most useful was that Sol could usually explain an implementation idea in a few paragraphs before we committed to it. That meant I could understand the tradeoffs well enough to make the call myself, even in areas where I’m definitely not an expert.

Another fun example was the wood material. I had a Blender shader I liked, and Sol helped me take it apart and rebuild the important parts in WGSL so the grain still makes sense when you cut into the wood and expose a completely new surface.

The project is currently Three.js + TypeGPU + WGSL.
